description: The Master System, the Game Gear and the SG-1000 through the console layer the apps use (ConsoleSessions.Create: the board session wrapped by the picture-chip bridge), headless via --console-run. Each case plays a game with a scripted pad and records the picture hash, the picture size, the number of distinct colours (the honesty check: a case whose picture is a flat colour proves nothing) and the audio peak (a game that made no sound shows 0). The goldens are what this build did when they were recorded after the same games were compared with Mesen 2.1.1 frame by frame (docs/projects/sega-track-a4.md): a green run says nothing moved, not that the emulation is right. Games are the user's library (X:\EMULATION; the cases skip on a machine without it); the SG-1000 programs and the tone-and-scroll program are written by the Workshop itself (--smstest --write-sg-programs / --write-swap-programs) into the 'gen' root, so no ROM of any kind is in the repository. Paths ending .7z# pick an entry of the archive by a piece of its name.

cases.description: Master System, the simplest roster game: title, then Galaxy Zone with fire held. Stock cores (Z80 / SMS / SMS).
Master System Sonic The Hedgehog: Green Hill, line-interrupt water and scroll effects, PSG music.
Master System Alex Kidd in Miracle World (v1.1): title, map, platforming.
Master System Micro Machines (Europe): the 50 Hz machine (the region comes from the file name through the app's factory), the Codemasters mapper, 224-line mode.
Master System Phantasy Star (Japan) on the Japanese sound unit SMS-FM (the game detects the YM2413 and plays its FM music); also a battery game.
Master System Wonder Boy III: The Dragon's Trap, with the menu script that gets past the title (New Game, the story, the castle).
Master System Sonic drawn by the enhanced NES picture chip FIXS (PPU menu id NES:FIXS): the picture bridge, at the Master System's own 256x192.

Master System Sonic with its PSG replayed on the NES FIX sound chip (APU menu id NES:FIX). Re-baselined 2026-10-29 (audio peak 13668 -> 13117, picture unchanged): APU_FIX no longer resets the triangle's step and timer on a $400B write (nesdev 'APU': there is no way to reset the triangle's phase). The Sega hub sends low PSG voices to the triangle and rewrites $400B whenever a note's period high bits change, so each such note change used to restart the triangle waveform at step 0 (a click and a phase jump); now the waveform runs on through the pitch change as on hardware. Isolated: a build with only the triangle fix gives exactly the new value; the same commit's sweep-mute fix alone changes nothing here.

Master System Sonic with every slot swapped while it runs (sound to SMS-FM, picture to NES:FIXS, sound to NES:FIX, picture and sound back to the console's own); all swaps must be in place and the game goes on.
Game Gear Sonic The Hedgehog: the 160x144 window, 12-bit colour, stereo PSG.
Game Gear Columns: tile rewrites during play, the game whose timing only matches the oracle with its own Z80 instruction lengths (this build keeps the Zilog ones).
Game Gear Wonder Boy: line-interrupt status bar.
Game Gear Shining Force II: 4 Mbit cartridge with battery RAM, intro dialogue.
cases.rom: {gg}/Shining Force II - The Sword of Hajya (U) [!].gg

cases.description: Game Gear Sonic with every slot swapped while it runs (sound to NES:FIXS, picture to NES:DMG, back to GG / GG); all swaps must be in place.

SG-1000 (TMS9918A Graphics II mode, magnified sprites): a hand-assembled program the Workshop writes (no real SG-1000 game exists in the library); the oracle's picture for the same program is pixel-identical (--smstest --only sg1000).
The assembled tone-and-scroll program of the hot-swap suite on a Master System: a steady 440 Hz PSG tone and a scrolling three-colour picture.
The same program on a Game Gear (stereo port opened).

Phantasy Star (USA, Europe) v1.3: an in-game save and a restart that loads it. Pass 1 plays the intro to the command menu (button 2 opens it, button 2 chooses, button 1 CANCELS), picks SAVE, slot 1, YES: the game writes slot 1 of its cartridge RAM. Pass 2 is a new session from that file: START / CONTINUE shows CONTINUE GAME, slot 1 loads and the game stands where it saved. The control run has no save file and cannot reach that picture.

Golden Axe Warrior: an in-game save and a restart that loads it. Pass 1 names the hero ABC, leaves the graveyard to the village, walks into the inn and talks to the keeper: 'You can save your game data here', YES (button 2 chooses, button 1 only moves the cursor), file 1. Pass 2 starts from that file: the title offers 'SELECT A FILE TO LOAD', file 1 shows ABC and loads the hero in the village at the inn.

Penguin Land: the stage editor's SAVE-01 / LOAD-01 (the game's only use of its battery besides the round select). Pass 1 opens the editor, takes the brick tool, places bricks and saves slot 1; pass 2 is a new session from that file: the editor's LOAD-01 puts the saved bricks back on the empty field. The control run (no file) loads nothing.

Defenders of Oasis (Game Gear): the game saves by itself when the throne-room conversation ends (slots 1 and 2 of its cartridge RAM go from the empty-slot fill to a record). Pass 2 is a new session from that file: the title menu offers New Game / Continue / Copy Game / Delete Game with Continue chosen, 'Which game will you continue from?' shows Game 1 LV 1 Chap. 1, and loading puts the prince in the throne room with control.

Shining Force II (Game Gear): an in-game save and a restart that loads it. Pass 1 (64,800 frames, the longest case: about a minute) plays the opening with button 2 taps and the first battle with a march macro (every unit's turn: four steps Down, confirm, BATT, confirm x3) until the hero falls at about frame 62,000; the priestess welcomes him back and the ring offers HELP / CHANGE / ITEM / SAVE: SAVE, 'May I record your adventures up to this point?' YES, 'Your adventure has been saved'. Pass 2 is a new session from that save file: the title menu offers START / CONT. / DEL. / COPY, CONT., story 1 ('1 AAAAAAAA BTL'), and the priestess welcomes the hero home with the ring back. The control run has no file: the story starts at once.
